messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 INCIDENT detected — outgoing rate limiter rollout (ratecap-v2) showing ~30-50% over-throttle on canary nodes in us-west-2. Symptoms: 429 spikes, customer latencies increase. Auto-pager -> alex (oncall).

alex (oncall): I'm on it. Acknowledge the page. Can someone pull up the canary cohort metrics and exemptions list?

mia (sre): looking now — dashboards show token_rejects rising at 14:12 UTC, coincident with deploy at 14:10. Canary is ~5% of traffic.

ravi (eng): quick context — this deploy turned on new exemption matching logic (exemptions-v2) to replace prefix-based rules. It shipped to canary only.

lina (cs): multiple customer support tickets incoming, several customers report sudden 429s and requests failing in their ingestion pipelines. One customer (AcmeAds) reports 40% of calls failing.

anja (product): (typo) sorry, meant anya — checking rollout notes: exemptions-v2 should preserve existing internal service exemptions, but there's a note that token-accounting shim was updated too.

ravi (eng): summary from my quick skim: exemptions-v2 regex order is reversed in the canary config, so some internal clients no longer match and get throttled. Also a token_count change in the middleware increments tokens for small heartbeats now. Possible double-count for certain GRPC keepalive paths.

alex (oncall): sounds like two failure modes: missing exemptions + token accounting inflation. Priority is mitigation. Options: 1) flip feature flag for ratecap-v2 off (kill-switch), 2) rollback canary deploy, 3) add temporary exemptions for internal clients via config. Thoughts?

pj (infra): we can flip the flag immediately with the feature flag service. Propagation ~15s. Rollback will take ~3-5m to rollback and re-deploy. Quick op: flip flag for canary group to old behavior.

ravi (eng): flip the flag first. I'll prepare a hotfix for the exemption order and token shim after we stabilize.

alex (oncall): do it. pj — please flip the flag and confirm metrics. Use `ff toggle ratecap-v2 canary=false --reason "rapid mitigation"` (runbook).

pj (infra): running now:```bash
ff toggle ratecap-v2 canary=false --reason "rapid mitigation"
```

pj (infra): flipped. Confirmed returned 200. Feature flag state: ratecap-v2 = OFF for canary.

mia (sre): metrics: token_rejects stopped rising within 45s, 429 rate trending down toward baseline. Latency normalizing.

lina (cs): telling AcmeAds and other affected customers we're rolling back the canary flag and that we expect requests to recover. They're happy to see progress — will monitor.

anya (product): nice. Do we need to escalate to SEs/customer success for impacted customers or loop in dedicated account owners?

lina (cs): looping SEs for top 3 impacted accounts, yes.

alex (oncall): good. Ravi — can you confirm root cause hypothesis and whether a rollback alone is sufficient?

ravi (eng): yes rollback (flag flip) removed the new matching logic; that prevents missed exemptions. But the token accounting bug is separate — it may cause higher unit usage and billing distortions if not fixed. I can push a patch to main that reorders the matchers and fixes the token shim, but will run through a smaller canary with extra gating.

mia (sre): recommend we also add a short-term compensating rule: add explicit exemptions for known internal prefixes as a guardrail in the legacy config while we fix v2. That way even if feature flag toggles flip unexpectedly, internal traffic is safe.

pj (infra): adding temporary exemptions now to legacy config. Patch applied, config reload in 12s.

pj (infra): reload complete. Verified internal call traces no longer show throttles.

alex (oncall): excellent. Monitoring shows healthy. I'm going to mark this as mitigated but still on incident state. We need postmortem and action items. Severity: S2 (customer-impacting but contained).

ravi (eng): I'll own the code fix. Plan: fix matching order + unit tests to cover negative/positive matches + address token_count increment drift. Will open PR and request expedited review.

mia (sre): I'll own the incident writeup and timeline. Will include play-by-play and script for ff toggle and temp exemptions.

lina (cs): I will compile list of impacted customers and customer-facing notes. We may offer credits if billing wrong due to token double-count.

anya (product): postmortem owner? mia? Also need to schedule a post-deploy checklist update to include canary gating for exemptions and token accounting smoke tests.

mia (sre): yes I'll coordinate the postmortem. Action items:
- ravi: PR with fix + canary + tests (target: +6h)
- pj: add monitoring alert for feature flag flips to canary (target: +24h)
- alex: update runbook to include step to add temp exemptions (target: +2h)
- lina: customer comms and potential billing remediation (target: +4h)
- mia: full incident report (target: EOD)

ravi (eng): PR created: `github.com/redwood/rl/PR#871` (draft). Adding unit tests for regex order and token shim.

pj (infra): logging an infra ticket to add FF audit webhooks so flips generate an audit page and pager if flipped outside scheduled windows.

alex (oncall): handing off to mia / next oncall. I'm leaving the channel, ping me if it regresses.

alex (oncall): next oncall is mia (sre) for the next 4 hours.

mia (sre): taking over. Thanks all. I'll consolidate notes and kick off postmortem doc.

lina (cs): thanks. customers report recovery. I'll keep monitoring for any billing anomalies.

incident-bot: INCIDENT status -> mitigated. Severity S2. Followup required.

mia (sre): final note — summary for postmortem: root cause = exemptions-v2 ordering change + token-accounting increment change introduced in same deploy; primary mitigation = feature flag flip + temp legacy exemptions; followups assigned.

pj (infra): added ticket INFRA-4321: "FF audit webhook + rollback fence"

ravi (eng): adding PR link in followup: https://github.com/redwood/rl/pull/871 — will request review from pj and alex.

mia (sre): postmortem doc link TBD. Owner: mia. Severity: S2. Close this thread once doc is published.

lina (cs): closing customer comm thread after all affected accounts confirm recovery.

pj (infra): one more ops note — we should consider a canary-run synthetic that simulates internal clients to catch exemptions drift in future canaries. Adding to infra backlog.

mia (sre): noted. OK I'll move this to followup list. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
